## Campaign rules (hypothesis.md, verbatim)

### Target buyer persona

**Who buys:** the owner of the declaration rules and of how height and weight are rated. At an insurer that is the head of underwriting (Diretor or Superintendente de Subscrição, Director de Suscripción, Director de Selección de Riesgos, Chief Underwriting Officer), the underwriting and acceptance managers who run the DPS and tele-interview routes, the medical director who decides what an estimate may be used for (Diretor Médico, Consultoria Médica, Director Médico, the head of medical underwriting or dictaminación médica), and the individual life, persons-insurance, product and actuarial heads who place the step in the application. In bancassurers, the life product heads. At reinsurers, the Latin American L&H underwriting, medical and client-underwriting heads. At Azos and Klimber, the founders and the heads of product and underwriting.

- **Why these titles, not others:** underwriting heads own the declaration limits and the rules that send a case to an exam; medical directors sign off on non-measured inputs; product, actuarial and individual life heads own the application and the extra premiums tied to height and weight. In Brazilian insurers the Diretor Técnico often owns underwriting and actuarial work: pulled, lane by scope. From the other §3 titles, innovation leads are pulled (P2 `proposition` with visible life scope, else P3 `referral`); CRO, population health, compliance and fraud-prevention teams are not (they do not own a case's evidence, and fraud framing is banned in copy). A bare product title at a multi-line insurer returns auto, home and health owners; life scope must be visible.
- **What they care about (KPIs):** share of cases accepted on the declaration or a tele-interview, with no exam; time to issue; evidence cost per case (medical exams, tele-interviews, lab tests); drop-off between quote and issue, with brokers, in bank branches and online; consistent, documented acceptance decisions; claims experience on declaration cases (never in copy).
- **Objections they will likely raise, with the honest answer:**
  - An estimate is not a weighing, and the typical gap is inside your error. True: Smart Scales is a software estimate at about 3.5% mean absolute error under evaluated conditions. The flag refers only gaps well above that, on the insurer's threshold; the rest stay on the declaration path.
  - Was it validated on our population? Validation participants were from the US and Europe; Brazilian and Mexican populations have not been characterized separately. A shadow evaluation on the insurer's own applicants measures it.
  - How many cases would that catch? Unknown until an evaluation on cases the insurer measures counts flags per threshold against the measured weight.
  - We would never accept or decline on photos. FitXpress does not make underwriting decisions; the insurer's rules and underwriters do.
  - Brokers and branch staff will not add a step. Under 45 seconds from the photos to structured results; the insurer decides where it is offered; the evaluation measures completion and retakes.
  - Where is the data, and what about LGPD or the Mexican data law? AWS, primarily US-West-2, partly US-East-1; photo handling as in `compliance.md`. No approved Brazilian or Mexican legal wording exists; these questions go to legal@3dlook.me (Open question 5).
  - Which insurers use it? None yet. The same capture, processing and integration run in production in remote BMI-verification and weight-management workflows; 3DLOOK has worked with 100+ clients.
  - Does it check height? No. Height comes from the application.
- **Tiers (order only; one import file):** P1 head of underwriting or acceptance (Diretor, Diretora, Superintendente or Head de Subscrição; Director or Directora de Suscripción or de Selección de Riesgos; Chief Underwriting Officer); chief or lead medical director at an insurer; head of individual life or persons insurance; at a reinsurer the Latin American L&H head, head of underwriting or medical director; founder, CEO, CPO or head of underwriting at group B. P2 underwriting and acceptance managers (Gerente, Gerente Executivo, Subdirector, Gerente de Suscripción), heads of medical underwriting or dictaminación, medical directors, life product heads, actuarial and pricing heads with life scope (`proposition`), Diretor Técnico with underwriting scope, bancassurance life product heads, innovation leads with visible life scope, client underwriting and L&H underwriting managers at reinsurers. P3 CTOs, CISOs, data protection officers (Encarregado de Proteção de Dados, Oficial de Protección de Datos), heads of product without life scope, group-wide innovation leads, a single-line insurer's CEO or COO where no underwriting owner is found. P4 referral.
- **Route-in below C-level (learnings PPL-1):** every IN account gets at least one P2 manager-level underwriting, medical or life product person when the export has one.
- **Lanes by title:** `underwriting` (underwriting, acceptance and risk-selection heads and managers, Diretor Técnico with underwriting scope); `medical` (CMOs, medical directors, Consultoria Médica, medical underwriting and dictaminación heads, at group C too); `proposition` (individual life, persons insurance, life product, actuarial and pricing, bancassurance life product, prestamista and habitacional heads, innovation heads with life scope, and group B founders and product heads); `reinsurance` (everyone else at group C except technology and privacy owners); `partnership` (Klimber only, if IN as a company that builds insurers' journeys); `technical-integration` (CTOs, architects, CISOs, data protection officers, digital channel technology owners); `referral` (anyone Vadim adds at step 4 from outside these functions, alliances and partnerships heads with digital scope, and group-wide innovation or transformation leads).
- **Location rule (step 4 applies it):** each person must be located in the row's country: Brazil rows in Brazil, Mexico rows in Mexico, Klimber in Argentina or Mexico. US-located people FAIL (nick's market; Miami-based Latin America heads included, count reported, Open question 11); Spain-located people FAIL (olena's market: Munich Re's Madrid L&H team, MAPFRE, BBVA and Zurich head offices; count reported); people located in Colombia, Chile, Peru, Central America or the Caribbean FAIL (outside the cut; count reported).
- **Not the buyer (FAIL, or a skipped pool at step 4):** individual underwriters and analysts (Analista de Subscrição, Subscritor, Suscriptor) and médicos dictaminadores unless the title says head, manager, coordinator, rules, innovation or automation; claims (Sinistros, Siniestros); sales, distribution, broker and branch network roles (Comercial, Vendas, Ventas, Canais, Canales, Agentes); anyone at a multi-line insurer outside life (auto, home and property, health plans and Gastos Médicos Mayores, dental, pensions and annuities, group benefits, large risks, rural, surety, investments); P&C staff at reinsurers.

### Anti-cases (where it does NOT work)

- **Group life, employee benefits and collective accident cover** (vida em grupo, seguro de vida grupo, colectivo): members are accepted within free-cover limits without individual height and weight.
- **Credit life and prestamista below the free-cover limit:** no individual DPS. Only cases where each borrower fills a DPS are in.
- **Health insurance and health plans** (Bradesco Saúde, SulAmérica Saúde, Gastos Médicos Mayores lines): a different use case; Brazilian health plans may not require a medical evaluation at enrolment (Idec).
- **Embedded micro-life, funeral and accident-only products** sold in apps, retail and payments: few or no health questions.
- **Pensions, savings and annuities** (previdência privada, rentas vitalicias).
- **Brokers, comparators and agencies that do not own the decision.** Azos and Klimber are in only because they run the decision journey.
- **Exam, lab and tele-interview vendors:** a later partner conversation.
- **Cases where an exam or a nurse actually measures height and weight** (usually the insurer's higher sums insured or a disclosed condition): the measurement is on file, and FitXpress adds nothing to it. These cases are the reference group of a shadow evaluation (Rules), never the use case. Tele-interview cases are not in this anti-case: height and weight there are stated, as on the declaration.
- **Recent deals within about 12 months** (`icp-detail.md` universal exclusion): Prudential do Brasil and Prudential Seguros México (CNP Assurances, signed 2026-10-20); Afirme Seguros (Talanx, May 2026); Seguros Banamex by default (Open question 4).
- **Entities and people outside Brazil and Mexico** (Klimber's Argentina head office excepted): Colombia, Chile, Peru, Central America, the Caribbean, Spain, the US.
- **Munich Re Automation Solutions** (`olena`'s) and any company already registered to another profile.
- **Any company whose application already runs a remote body, face or BMI-from-image capture:** held for Vadim.

## What past campaigns taught (learnings.md 2026-10-30, verbatim)

Campaign rules above win over these. `[directional]` is the default; say why when you depart from it. `[watch]` is not a rule yet.

### People

**PPL-1 [directional] Seniority runs backwards.** C-level and founders replied to 5/344
invites, everyone below them to 37/1064. The validator's P1 tier: 2/200; P3 and P4 together:
29/671. Keep decision-makers on the list, but do not give P1 for title alone, and give every IN
account at least one route-in below C-level (programme, clinical, practitioner or partnerships
lead) when the export has one. Part of the gap is C-level people not accepting strangers'
invites; the rates are per invite.

**PPL-2 [directional] The referral ask is a way in.** `referral` lane: 21/475 replied; buyer
lanes: 21/958. Referral replied at least as often as buyer lanes in 5 of the 6 campaigns that
had both. A non-buyer at an IN account in a relevant function is a referral-lane PASS, not a FAIL.

**PPL-3 [directional] Functions that do not answer.** Per person contacted: marketing 0/52,
retention / CRM / growth 0/44, non-clinical operations 0/55, engineering 1/90. Partnerships, BD
and sales: 6/83, the highest. Clinical operations titles count as clinical, not operations.
Do not fill an account's cap with marketing, CRM or engineering people.

**PPL-4 [directional] Who the positive repliers were.** Of 34 positive repliers, 3 were C-level.
The rest: coaching lead, Tier 3 practitioner lead, obesity consultant, dietitian, clinical
operations lead, head of commercial, regional partnerships manager, director of clinical
programmes, senior director of clinical research, GM health and wellbeing.

**PPL-5 [watch] Stale contacts.** 5/72 repliers had left the company on the list. Checked
2026-10-30: of the four that can be traced, two came from Sales Navigator exports with no role
start date and one from Apollo with a role started in 2009 (a recent leaver). A filter on
Apollo's role start date would have caught none of them, so there is no filter. A leaver who
names a successor is a referral.

## ICP segment (icp-detail.md, verbatim)

### 3. Life & Disability Insurance Underwriting

**What they are:** life insurers, disability insurers, group benefits carriers, digital insurance / insurtech platforms, реinsurers, preventive-health risk-assessment компании, AI-driven underwriting/claims платформы, population health analytics providers — верифицируют body metrics при заявке.

**Buyer titles:**
- Chief Underwriting Officer / VP Underwriting
- Chief Medical Officer
- Head of Risk & Analytics / Chief Risk Officer
- Head of Digital Innovation / Digital Transformation Leader
- Product / Innovation Manager
- Insurtech Strategy Team
- Population Health Director
- CTO
- Compliance & Fraud Prevention Team

**Company size & revenue:** large enterprise (обычно 5K+ сотрудников), **$5M+ annual revenue** — компании, андеррайтящие большие популяции или модернизирующие digital enrollment/verification.

**Geo:** US (Prudential, MetLife, Guardian Life, New York Life, Lincoln Financial), EU/UK (Aviva UK, Legal & General UK, Allianz DE, AXA FR, Generali IT), плюс Canada, UAE, Australia.

**Pain points — Underwriting:**
- Ненадёжный self-reported BMI/вес
- Медленные ручные процессы, friction/задержки в очном screening
- Нет масштабируемой, defensible remote-верификации
- Рост издержек с объёмом, плохой enrollment experience

**Pain points — Operational & Risk:**
- Административная нагрузка ручной верификации здоровья
- Сложно консистентно оценивать распределённые популяции
- Фрод и несогласованные submissions
- Нужна автоматизация без потери compliance

**KPIs:** underwriting cycle time (дни), application completion rate / drop-off, discrepancy / rework rate, audit readiness.

**Triggers:**
- Digital transformation инициатива
- Переход на no-medical-exam underwriting tier
- Re-platforming / новая policy admin система
- Давление модернизировать enrollment для конкуренции с digital-first insurtech

**Hero message hook:** "Verify body metrics remotely to issue faster, cut rework, and strengthen auditability."

**Critical for outbound:** лидировать HIPAA/GDPR + audit logs + workflow integration. НЕ точностью как таковой. Они ценят defensibility.

**Examples to target (verify status before outreach):**
- Health & Life Insurance: UnitedHealthcare, Humana, Cigna, Aetna, Prudential, MetLife, Guardian Life, New York Life, Lincoln Financial
- Insurtech & Digital: Oscar Health, Lemonade, Alan
- Wellness & Preventive: Vitality, Personify Health
- EU/UK: Aviva UK, Legal & General UK, Allianz DE, AXA FR, Generali IT
